thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: S&P 500, Nasdaq Look To Snap 4-day Losing Streak; Energy Among Biggest Gainers

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: S&P 500, Nasdaq Look To Snap 4-day Losing Streak; Energy Among Biggest Gainers
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
All 11 S&P 500 sectors are higher
U.S. stocks rose in early trading on Monday, in a partial rebound from the steep decline suffered at the end of last week.
The day's gains were broad-based, with all 11 of the S&P 500's primary industry groups in positive territory. Energy stocks were among the biggest gainers, with the sector up 0.9%.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 82 points, or 0.3%, to 25,995. The S&P 500 was up 11 points to 2,882, a gain of 0.4%. The Nasdaq Composite Index gained 12 points, or 0.2%, to 7,914.
Both the S&P and the Nasdaq are coming off four straight daily declines. Last week was the S&P's first negative week of the past four, and it represented the biggest weekly percentage drop since June. The Nasdaq suffered its biggest weekly drop since March.
The three gauges are showing year-to-date gains ranging from 5.2% to nearly 15%.
What's driving markets?
Recent market activity has been driven in part by uncertainty surrounding trade policy between the U.S. and its major trading partners. President Donald Trump recently threatened China with the latest in a series of tariffs, which would impact an additional $267 billion in Chinese goods. This comes on top of an already-proposed $200 billion in tariffs.
Investors are concerned that such measures, especially if they are met with retaliatory actions by other countries, could spiral into a full-on trade war, one that could have negative implications for global economic growth.
Technology stocks have also driven trading of late, with the sector--by far the strongest performer thus far this year--seeing steep losses last week. The group can be sensitive to trade issues. Over the weekend, Trump published a tweet urging (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-urges-apple-to-move-manufacturing-to-the-us-2018-09-08)Apple Inc.(AAPL) to shift production out of China to the U.S.
Apple said tariffs against China would impact a "wide range" of its products (http://www.marketwatch.com/press-release/united-states-apple-says-us-tariffs-on-china-would-hit-wide-range-of-products-2018-09-09).
What are strategists saying?
"U.S. markets look set for a modest rebound on the open after last week's selloff, despite the ratcheting up of trade tensions by President Trump over the weekend," said Michael Hewson, chief market analyst, at CMC Markets UK in a note.
Which stocks are in focus?
Shares in Apple were down 1.1% in the wake of Trump's comments.
Tesla Inc. shares (TSLA) rose 3.3% after CEO Elon Musk announced a management shake-up (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musk-shakes-up-tesla-management-after-key-departures-2018-09-07) late Friday. That move came after the car maker's stock slumped in Friday's session as more executives departed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musks-high-and-teslas-low-stock-and-bonds-tumble-on-ceos-latest-shenanigans-2018-09-07) and Musk appeared to smoke marijuana during an interview (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musk-appears-to-smoke-marijuana-during-an-interview-2018-09-07-51033514).
Science Applications International Corp.(SAIC) on Monday said it would buy Engility Holdings Inc.(EGL) in a stock deal valued at $2.5 billion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/saic-to-buy-engility-in-a-stock-deal-valued-at-25-billion-including-debt-2018-09-10), including the repayment of $900 million in debt. Shares of Science Applications fell 7.8% while Engility rose 1%.
United Rentals Inc. (URI) said it would buy BlueLine Rental in a cash deal valued at $2.1 billion. Shares of United rose 3.7%.
Snap Inc.(SNAP) fell 1.5% after the company said its chief strategy officer would be the latest executive to leave the company (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/snap-chief-strategy-officer-imran-khan-is-latest-exec-to-leave-to-pursue-other-opportunities-2018-09-10).
Shares in Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.(BABA) fell 2.3% following news that tycoon Jack Ma plans to step down as executive chairman (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/alibabas-jack-ma-likely-to-unveil-succession-plan-monday-2018-09-09) of the Chinese e-commerce giant in a year.
CBS Corp.'s stock (CBSA) fell 2.6% after Les Moonves, the longtime chairman and CEO, resigned Sunday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-chief-les-moonves-reportedly-will-resign-amid-new-sexual-misconduct-accusations-2018-09-09) following new sexual misconduct allegations against him from six additional women.
Which economic reports are getting attention?
Boston Federal Reserve President Eric Rosengren said, in an interview with MarketWatch (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/feds-rosengren-says-yield-curve-is-not-an-important-indicator-2018-09-10), that he doesn't read much about the danger of a possible recession (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/feds-rosengren-says-yield-curve-is-not-an-important-indicator-2018-09-10)from the shape of the yield curve,. He also said financial risks now are coming from smaller banks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/boston-fed-president-says-financial-risks-now-coming-from-smaller-banks-2018-09-10).
Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic is also slated to make remarks, speaking at an event in Georgia at noon Eastern Time.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
An August survey of consumer expectations is slated to hit at 11 a.m. Eastern, and a July reading on consumer credit is expected at 3 p.m. Eastern.
What are other markets doing?
Stocks in Asia fell after Trump's comment on Apple's production, which put some pressure on Asian tech stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-stocks-dip-after-trumps-apple-production-comments-2018-09-09). European stocks were modestly higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stoxx-europe-600-edges-higher-shaking-off-swedens-election-results-2018-09-10).
Treasury prices held their ground (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/treasury-yields-steady-as-investors-eye-tariff-developments-2018-09-10), keeping yields steady, as traders watched for U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports that could arrive this week.
Oil futures ticked higher, buoyed by continued concerns (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-finds-footing-as-investors-eye-iran-sanctions-2018-09-10) over the impact of renewed sanctions on Iran and signs of a pickup in crude demand from China.
